note: Montserrat, read in the Revised Laws the Government of Montserrat publishes on gov.ms (2026-10-31). Majority: no Act setting the age of majority or a minor's capacity to contract was found among the revised laws gov.ms serves (its media library searched for majority, minor, infant, age and contracts; Chapter 5 holds the Marriage Act, the Children (Care and Adoption) Act, the Guardianship of Infants Act and the Status of Children Act, none of which sets it); the Children (Care and Adoption) Act calls a child a person under 18 and the Marriage Act (as at 1 January 2025) asks consent to marry under 18, but neither is a rule of full capacity, so majority is null. Work: the Labour Code (Cap. 15.03, as at 1 January 2025), s. 2, calls a child a person under 16 and a young person one of 16 or 17, and s. 91 bars employing a child, save light work the Minister approves from 14, school and reformatory work and a non-dangerous family undertaking (not held); young persons are barred from ships (s. 92) and night work and dangerous machines (ss. 94, 97, 110), not held. Performers: s. 91(3)(b) excepts artistic performances approved by the Minister, on conditions the Governor sets on Cabinet's advice, so performers under 16 need the Minister's approval; no lowest age is set. Service: the National Service Act (Cap. 10.16, Acts 5 of 1939, 24 of 1982 and 9 of 2011, revised edition as at 1 January 2013, still in the 2026 revised laws) makes every male Montserratian ordinarily resident in Montserrat from 18 until he turns 55 liable for national service in Montserrat (s. 2), called by the Governor's written notice or a notice in the Gazette for as long as he deems necessary (s. 4), with exemptions on application (s. 3) and the Schedule's exceptions; no term is set, so months is null. No call-up in force was looked for or found: the liability is the law's, and how often it is used isn't known (a reading to check). The Montserrat Defence Force itself is voluntary (Defence Force Act, Cap. 10.07, s. 4).
